title: Field Labs: Deployment Sprint Map & Risk Register
body:
Purpose:
This working doc maps out a compact, customer-facing POC (Field Labs) sprint for validating Redwood Inference deployments in a constrained production-like environment. It combines a timeboxed plan, explicit owner matrix, a prioritized risk register with mitigation owners, and a pared-down runbook for the first 30 days post-deploy.

Context and constraints:
- Customer: Midwest Fintech (PII-sensitive workflows).
- Primary objective: Prove 99th percentile latency < 220ms for request sizes up to 1024 tokens under representative concurrency.
- Environment: Dedicated VPC deployment (private), single-region (us-west2), mixed-model routing (gpt-rlf-ensemble + quantized v2 candidate).
- Hard constraints: no external internet egress for inference nodes; KMS-managed keys; SOC2 audit window aligned with week 4.

Success criteria (must be measurable):
1) Latency SLO met: 99th percentile < 220ms for token length distribution profile A during a 30-minute soak at target qps.
2) Cost baseline: token-cost per 1M tokens <= $X (customer target) with recommended batching/quantization applied.
3) Data controls validated: access logs present, KMS key rotation tested, and blind tokenization applied for PII flows.
4) Rollout readiness: Canary policy and rollback tested in two simulated failure modes.

High-level sprint map (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (Prep, 3 days): kickoff, infra sketch, ticketing, baseline perf tests on a staging model variant. Owner: Maya Chen.
- Week 1 (Deploy + Instrument): provision VPC cluster, install private control plane, integrate KMS, deploy initial model variant, enable tracing & metrics. Owner: Infrastructure lead (Diego).
- Week 2 (Workloads + Tuning): run representative workloads, collect latency/cost metrics, apply batching and KV cache tuning, iterate kernel selection. Owner: Applied ML (Anya).
- Week 3 (Faulting + Rollouts): run chaos experiments (node OOM, network flaps), validate fallback to quantized model variant and cross-region fallback, test canary. Owner: SRE (Liam).
- Week 4 (Handover + Audit prep): collate runbook, finalize acceptance report, provide ops workshop and transfer runbooks to customer. Owner: Solutions Eng (Priya).

Roles & Responsibilities (short):
- Solutions Eng (Maya): overall PO, delivery cadence, customer syncs, escalation owner.
- Infrastructure (Diego): VPC, compute, KMS, networking and peering config.
- Applied ML (Anya): model variant config, quantization tuning, perf verification.
- SRE (Liam): monitoring, alerting playbooks, chaos verification.
- Customer Eng contact: Sarah Blake (customer) - environment creds and workload samples.

Prioritized risk register (top 8):
1) KMS integration delays (Impact: high, Likelihood: medium). Mitigation: parallelize KMS onboarding with test tokenization stub; Owner: Diego.
2) Model variant mismatch causing quality regressions (Impact: high, Likelihood: medium-high). Mitigation: hold prompt evasion test suite; Owner: Anya.
3) Network egress policy blocks required telemetry (Impact: medium, Likelihood: medium). Mitigation: pre-approve telemetry endpoints and use VPC peering test; Owner: Diego.
4) Autoscaler thrash under burst (Impact: medium, Likelihood: medium). Mitigation: conservative autoscale ramp and synthetic load tests; Owner: Liam.
5) Cost overshoot in tuning loop (Impact: medium, Likelihood: medium-high). Mitigation: guardrails in experiments, nightly cost reports; Owner: Maya.
6) Lack of customer test data quality (Impact: high, Likelihood: medium). Mitigation: provide anonymized workload generator and sample mapping guide; Owner: Priya.
7) Image compatibility on customer infra (Impact: medium, Likelihood: low). Mitigation: pre-flight hardware/driver checklist; Owner: Infrastructure.
8) Audit evidence gaps (Impact: high, Likelihood: low-medium). Mitigation: early engagement with compliance, capture logs during Week 2 soak; Owner: Maya/Priya.

Runbook skeleton (for handover):
- Pre-deploy checklist: subnet allocation, routes, security groups, KMS key created, AMIs validated, firewall rules.
- Deploy steps: install agent, register with control plane, pull model bundle, run model smoke test.
- Validation steps: execute perf harness with workload profile A, collect traces, compare against baseline.
- Rollbacks: step-by-step to switch traffic to quantized fallback + scale-up recipe.
- Incident playbook: 5-min triage, escalate to SRE, snapshot logs, attach to incident ticket.

Workshop plan (90 minutes, week 4 handover):
1) 10m: Recap of objectives and success metrics.
2) 20m: Live demo — warm path, cold path, KV cache show-and-tell.
3) 25m: Walkthrough of runbook and canary policy.
4) 20m: Troubleshooting lab — guided exercises (alert -> remediation).
5) 15m: Next steps and Q&A.

Checklist: (quick status markers)
- [ ] Kickoff scheduled and calendar invites sent.
- [x] Pre-flight security questionnaire submitted.
- [x] Customer provided sample workload (anonymized) v1.
- [ ] KMS test key integrated in staging.
- [ ] Canary policy drafted.
- [ ] Cost guardrails configured in Redwood Console.

Open questions / decisions to resolve before Week 1:
- Can customer accept our telemetry endpoints for tracing and SLO collection? (Action: Maya to confirm).
- Are there approved HSM/KMS ARNs for production keys or do we operate with staged keys first? (Action: Diego).
- Confirm preferred rollback window and maintenance window for canary traffic shift. (Action: Customer + Maya).

Attachments & artifacts to finalise:
- Minimal perf harness repo (linked_artifacts above).
- Prompt evasion test suite + golden prompts (Confluence PL ticket).
- VPC pre-flight checklist spreadsheet (depot: shared drive).

Next steps (next 72h):
1) Maya to run kickoff call and create JIRA epic and tickets (JIRA-SEQ-4128).
2) Diego to spin up staging network and provide test KMS key stub.
3) Anya to run baseline model perf and publish initial token-cost numbers.
4) Priya to produce the 90m workshop deck draft for handover.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep bench perf tests cheap: use quantized small-batch runs before scaling up.
- Watch out for GPU driver mismatches in customer infra, we lost 6 hours last time.
- Consider adding a short latency SLI dashboard tile in Redwood Console specifically for this POC.

Revision history:
- 2025-10-02: initial outline and objectives (Maya).
- 2025-10-08: added risk register and week-by-week tasks (team).
- 2025-10-14: updated runbook skeleton and workshop agenda (in review).

This document is a living working doc — expect frequent updates as we run the first soak and gather data.
